rule.body: With 'either...or' and 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'As well as', 'together with' and 'along with' do not change the subject. 'The number of' is singular; 'a number of' is plural. Words like 'news' and 'mathematics' are singular. An amount of time or money seen as one whole takes a singular verb. A group noun acting as one unit, shown by words like 'its', takes a singular verb.
rule.example: Neither the principal nor the teachers were at the gate.

questions.stem: The news from the hospital ___ very encouraging today.
questions.explanation: 'News' ends in -s but it is singular, so it takes the singular verb 'is'.

questions.stem: Mathematics ___ the subject Tunde enjoys most.
questions.explanation: 'Mathematics' is the name of one subject, so it is singular and takes 'is'.

questions.stem: Either Tunde or his sisters ___ going to cook tonight.
questions.explanation: With 'either...or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'His sisters' is plural, so we use 'are'.

questions.stem: A number of students ___ absent from the lecture yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' means 'many', so the subject is plural. The time is past, so the verb is 'were'.

questions.stem: The number of cars on Lagos roads ___ increasing every year.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' refers to one figure, so it is singular and takes 'is'.

questions.stem: The principal, as well as the teachers, ___ attending the meeting.
questions.explanation: 'As well as the teachers' is extra information. The subject is 'The principal', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.

questions.stem: Ten years ___ a long time to wait for a promotion.
questions.explanation: 'Ten years' here is one period of time seen as a whole, so it takes the singular verb 'is'.

questions.stem: Neither the boys nor their father ___ at home when the visitors arrived.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Their father' is singular and the time is past, so 'was'.

questions.stem: The committee ___ its decision after a long meeting.
questions.explanation: The word 'its' shows the committee is acting as one unit, so it takes a singular verb: 'has announced'.

questions.stem: Ngozi, along with her two cousins, ___ expected at the wedding tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'Along with her two cousins' does not change the subject. 'Ngozi' is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
